### What to build (Spud's design; refine it only with a reason in your Result)
- **Count each request once.** Group a transcript's assistant entries by request: `message.id`, with `requestId` when present; an entry with neither is its own request. Take each request's last entry's usage. On the real transcripts the last entry is the maximum on every key and only `output_tokens` grows; if you find a later entry lower on some key, take the per-key maximum and say so. `messages` counts requests. Tool uses count distinct `tool_use` block ids across all entries (a block without an id counts where it appears), so the count is right whether the harness writes one block per entry or all blocks in one. Duration stays first to last timestamp.
- **Mark the new counting.** A new sum's `usage_json` carries a marker (Spud's default: `"counting": "request"`), so a sum made the old way, without it, can be found. `token_counts`, the card and the member note read both shapes as they do today; SPD-021's `completion` block and `run_totals` merge are unchanged.
- **Re-sum stored rows with a Spud-only command.** Spud's default: `spud --as spud member resum <ref>... | --all [--dry-run]`. For each member whose `usage_json` is a transcript sum without the marker:
  - Resolve its transcript: the recorded `transcript_path` when it is a file; else the file with the same session directory and file name under any project directory beside the recorded one. The harness moves a worktree session's transcripts into the main project directory after `ExitWorktree`: four of the five recorded paths are gone today, and each file is at `~/.claude/projects/-Users-ericlugo-Personal-Spud/<session>/subagents/agent-<agent_id>.jsonl`. Exactly one match, or the member is reported as not found.
  - Re-sum it with the new counting and merge through `run_totals`, so a completion kept by SPD-021 keeps its whole-run duration and tool count; set `transcript_path` to the file read.
  - Write one event per member with the old and new `total_tokens`, `tool_uses` and `duration_ms` and the old `usage_json` whole.
  - `--dry-run` prints the same table and writes nothing; a second run changes nothing, because of the marker. An imported sum (`imported: true`, no transcript) and a member whose transcript cannot be found or read are listed and left as they are; decide the exit code and write it down. Any actor but Spud is refused with exit 3.
- **Hooks count the new way** through `transcript_usage`; SPD-021's rule that a stored sum is not summed again at a stop stays.
- Docstrings and help name the counting.

Decisions the brief left open.
1. Grouping key: (message.id, requestId or None). An entry without a message id is a request of its own even when it has a requestId (proof 3 counts entries without a message id once each). On the five live transcripts message ids and requestIds pair 1:1 (177 requests), so message.id alone would give the same sums; I kept the brief's pairing, pinned by test_the_request_is_the_message_id_with_its_request_id.
2. Last entry, no per-key maximum: in 177 of 177 live requests the last entry is the maximum on every key; only output_tokens varies (in 164 requests), and it never decreases.
3. Marker: "counting": "request" beside source, messages and usage. stored_counting reads a stored sum as request, imported (imported: true, never re-summed) or entry (neither, so before SPD-023). token_counts, the card and the note read every shape as before.
4. Command and selection: member resum. --all takes every member whose usage_json has source transcript, in ticket then lineage order; named refs take any member, deduplicated. Each member gets an action: re-sum; counted, imported or no sum (nothing to do); not found, ambiguous, unreadable or no usage (left).
5. Output: a table (member, action, requests, total_tokens old -> new, tool_uses, duration_ms, and transcript as recorded: or moved: with the path, or the note), then one line: "re-summed N of M members once per API request; ..." or "dry run, nothing written: would re-sum ...". --json: dry_run, members [{ref, action, found, transcript, note, requests, old, new}], resummed, left.
6. Exit codes: 0 when every listed member is re-summed, counted, imported or has no sum; 1 when any sum that added every entry is left (not found, ambiguous, unreadable, no usage), with the others still written in the same transaction, as render writes the rest and exits 6; --dry-run exits the same; 2 for neither or both of refs and --all; 3 for any actor but Spud (require_spud). The table goes to stdout, and a spud: line naming each left member to stderr.
7. Event: kind member.edited rather than a new kind, since the events kind CHECK would need a migration of the append-only table; actor spud; a body with the old -> new figures; data {fields (the changed columns), counting, found, transcript, requests, old and new: {total_tokens, tool_uses, duration_ms, transcript_path, usage_json as the stored text}}.
8. Transcript search: the recorded path when it is a file; else <projects>/*/<session>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl beside the recorded project directory, exactly one match; only that subagent layout is searched. Transcripts are read before the write lock is taken; the write re-reads each row, merges through run_totals, and skips a row a concurrent run has already re-summed.
